To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the effects of a worksite SMT intervention on psychological strain, emotional and depersonalized burnout are enhanced when employees have low levels of work self-efficacy, and (b) this effect is enhanced when employees have high levels of intrinsic motivation.
work-related self-efficiency is an important factor in determining the impact of a worksite stress-management training (SMT).
work-related self-efficiency and intrinsic work motivation may moderate the effects of a worksite stress intervention.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of a worksite stress-management training intervention on the work-related self-efficiency and work motivation of U.K. government workers.
work-related self-efficiency as a moderator of the impact of a worksite stress-management training (SMT).
the role of work-related selfefficacy as a moderator of the effects of a worksite stress-management training (SMT), in relation to intrinsic work motivation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present study provided evidence for the proposition that the benefits of a SMT intervention are conditional upon employees also having high baseline levels of work motivation.

the present study has demonstrated a significant higher order interaction effect on emotional exhaustion (i.e., Group × Time 1 Self-Efficacy X Time 1 In-Motivation), but not on depersonalization, and not for any of the other variables examined in the present study.

the results of the study support the proposition that the low work-related self-efficiency/enhanced SSM training benefits effect is conditional on employees having high levels of intrinsically motivated work.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
employees with low levels of self-efficacy for their work, but who also have a high intrinsic motivation for their work, may stand to benefit the most from a worksite SMT intervention.
employees with lower levels of work-related efficacy, and who have high levels of intrinsic motivation, are likely to benefit more from SMT interventions.
work-related self-efficiency is a significant predictor of psychological strain and work-related stress, and is also an important factor in determining the effectiveness of a SMT intervention.
The main takeaway from our work is that
employees who are low in work-related self-eﬃcacy and high in intrinsic work motivation stand to benefit the most from a worksite SMT intervention.

the effectiveness of SMT interventions can be enhanced by targeting individuals with low work-related self efficacy and high intrinsic work motivation, as these are the individuals most likely to benefit from SMT.
employees with low levels of intrinsic work-related motivation may stand to benefit from a stress management training intervention.
